note: Adapted from the new-species description of Sands 1965 (type locality Bolgatanga, Ghana), in English; the alate and the soldier are described, with no separate worker. The OCR mistook decimal points for hyphens or colons (0:93 is 0.93, "760-8-60" is 7.60—8.60), restored here by order of magnitude.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Larger than E. bipartitus, with a differently shaped frontal mark, a more strongly inflated postclypeus and compound eyes that do not protrude from the sides of the head as markedly; the soldier cannot be distinguished from that of E. bipartitus and the two are separable only by distribution. The alate ocelli lie closer to the eye than in E. convergens, and the postclypeus is less inflated than in E. convergens; E. undulans is smaller with the frontal mark nearly effaced, and E. abruptus has smaller ocelli lying farther from the eye; in the soldier only 1—2 pairs of setae stand behind the postcranial constriction, whereas the other species have 3—5 pairs.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark brown, with pale yellowish brown patches on the frons, the postclypeus and the antennae, labrum yellow; pronotum brown, meso- and metanotum and femora yellowish brown, tibiae and tarsi yellow; abdominal tergites brown, sternites yellowish brown; wing membrane translucent, very pale brown, veins brown. Posterior margin of the head capsule behind the eyes rounded, the sides more strongly arcuate, slightly flared at the eye margin; frontal mark pale, irregularly bilobed, with a triangular middle part, the lateral arms variable in length and shape and sometimes separate from it; compound eyes hardly protruding from the sides of the head, oval, eye width index 2.5—2.8; ocelli large, oval, separated from the compound eye by less than one third of their minimum diameter; postclypeus strongly inflated, 1.8—1.9 times as wide as long, anterior margin straight, posterior margin convex and arched in the middle, wavy near the outer corners; antennae 15-segmented, segments II, IV and V subequal, III very small. Head setae fairly uniform and dense, not yet forming a fur. Measurements (8 individuals, 2 localities, mm): head width (across the eyes) 0.93—0.99 (mean 0.94); maximum diameter of the compound eye 0.34—0.38 (mean 0.36); ocellus 0.10—0.11 × 0.14—0.16 (mean 0.10 × 0.15); ocellus to eye 0.02—0.03 (mean 0.02); pronotum width 0.71—0.78 (mean 0.74); pronotum length 0.50—0.56 (mean 0.53); hind tibia length 1.08—1.20 (mean 1.12); forewing length 7.60—8.60 (mean 8.12).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow to yellow, nasus orange yellow to orange, the rest of the body wall pale yellow. Head capsule in frontal view hardly constricted behind the antennae, the posterior margin slightly angularly rounded; nasus rather stout, weakly conical. In lateral view almost a straight line or slightly convex, the base of the nasus sometimes weakly raised; antennal segments II, III and V subequal, IV shorter. The conspicuous head setae are 3 pairs (6 in all) in a transverse row at the constriction in front of the base of the nasus, and 1—2 pairs on the vertex behind the constriction. Measurements (8 individuals, 2 localities, mm): head length (to the tip of the nasus) 1.28—1.38 (mean 1.32); head width 0.60—0.65 (mean 0.62); head capsule depth 0.39—0.45 (mean 0.41); pronotum width 0.35; pronotum length 0.13; hind tibia length 0.68—0.70 (mean 0.70).
